paper.title: Algorithm 453: Gaussian Quadrature Formulas for Bromwich's Integral
paper.venue: Communications of the ACM 16(8), August 1973, pp. 486-487 (the archive header 453.gz says CACM vol. 16 no. 8 Aug 1973 pp. 486-487). The frame lists it as TOMS 16,8 and R. Diessens; the frame's venue and author spelling are not the archive's. Paper text not checked: it is paywalled.

code.commit: netlib TOMS archive 453.gz (scouted 2026-11-27, gz sha256 57563056450e03c510b778971d7539577da3f3e962cf5ce1650507466121b9f7). Shell archive unpacks to Fortran/Sp/{Makefile,driver.f,res,src.f} (BROMIN and its routines in src.f, driver TOMS453_PRB with test01).

claim.location: Shipped reference file Fortran/Sp/res (inside 453.gz): the printed output of driver.f subroutine TEST01 for N=6 and S=0.0, which calls BROMIN and prints the complex abscissas XR, XI and weights WR, WI (format g14.6). The three printed rows of that block are the claimed values.
claim.metric: The 12 printed numbers of the first TEST01 block (N = 6, S = 0.00000): XR, XI, WR, WI for each of the three printed abscissas, in the order printed.
claim.paper_value: Not located in the paper text (paywalled; Burkardt and Netlib index describe the algorithm as a program, and no printed table of abscissas was found). The archive's res file is the only value to check.

tolerance.basis: Fixed before any run. The reference prints 6 significant digits (g14.6), so the largest magnitude printed here is 315.065, whose last printed unit is 0.001 (rounding half-unit 0.0005). A tolerance of 1e-3 allows one unit in the last printed place at the largest magnitude, and no more. It does not allow a different root or weight set. Not loosened after any run.

cost.cpu_minutes_estimate: Under 1 minute for TEST01 (the driver runs many N and S values; only the first block is claimed). Needs a Fortran 77/90 compiler; gfortran is not on this host's PATH.
cost.data_licence: Not stated in the archive; a CACM algorithm published with the ACM. The rerun should record the licence it finds.

why: The shipped driver calls BROMIN to compute a complex Gaussian quadrature rule for Bromwich's integral; the printed abscissas and weights depend on the root-finding and recurrence in the code and cannot be read off the paper.
